newsitem.title: USA: Rykoff, JP deal seen facing no problems-arbs.
newsitem.headline: Rykoff, JP deal seen facing no problems-arbs.

text.p: The $1.4 billion merger agreement between Rykoff-Sexton Inc and JP Foodservice Co announced Monday morning will face little difficulty reaching consummation, arbitrageurs said.

Shareholders representing about 36 percent of Rykoff have agreed to back the deal; and there is no share-price collar that could pressure the pact if the two stock prices rose or fell sharply, so the companies' year-end completion goal would likely be reached, they said.
"This one looks pretty plain vanilla" with no outstanding issues, said an arb who declined to be identified.

Under the agreement, unanimously approved by both boards of directors, JP and Rykoff would merge in a tax-free exchange of shares under which Rykoff holders would get 0.84 JP share for each Rykoff share held, they said.
JP stock closed NYSE trade Friday at 30-1/8, while Rykoff finished the week at 19-5/8.
Based on these prices and the terms of the agreement, Rykoff shares are valued at about $25.30 per share.
The $1.4 billion total includes the assumption of about $700 million in Rykoff debt, the companies said.
The merged entity would be called JP Foodservice Inc, and the companies claim it would be the second largest foodservice company in the United States, with annual sales of $5.2 billion.
